title: 14 rounds of AI art review on my game's fog. The reviewers kept flipping between "too milky" and "invisible", and the fix wasn't a slider
author: idlerunner00
selftext:
Out of Pixkrieg is my extraction RTS, and everything in it is generated in code, the light included. For shadows and fog I let agents iterate on their own for about six hours: one agent implements, a fresh reviewer agent scores the result, the findings go back.

The setup that made it work:

* captures come from the real game renderer on a fixed test world. No image edits, nothing generated
* every review image shows the old version above and the new one below, as 1:1 crops, six views per round
* a new reviewer for every round, with the previous findings as text only
* the same test logs the GPU time of every render pass, so a prettier change can't quietly be a slower one

Scores out of 10 from some of the rounds (some rounds stale):

|Round|Mist|Overall|
|:-|:-|:-|
|0 (old light)|1|3.5|
|1|2.5|3.5 to 4|
|5|3|5.5|
|6|5.5|6|
|9|5|7|
|10|5.5|6.5|
|14|7.5|8|

What I learned:

* The flip-flop was the most useful signal. Round 1: a uniform milky veil. Round 5: the fog banks were invisible. Round 6: visible for the first time, but as a milky wash over everything. Round 9: too restrained again. Turning the density up and down was never going to converge. What worked was changing the structure: fog in banks with clear air between them, thinning with height and keeping the colour of whatever it covers.
* Reviewers are noisy. They rescored the unchanged old version anywhere between 4 and 5 for light. That's why the old version is in every single image.
* Visual review finds technical bugs. Horizontal stripes on cliff faces turned out to be the air grid storing heights in 8 bits, so the fog stepped every 8 pixels. The reviewer only saw stripes, the agent traced them to the cause.
* Check the views you didn't target. Round 13 looked shippable, but in the zoomed out strategy view the fog banks became white smudges. Round 14 fixed only that.
* And it got faster on the way: the new light takes 26 to 36% less GPU time than the old one in my native benchmark.
* Plan the content pipeline into developing your project. I did so and now have a easy way of creating before / after clips and showcase stuff that changed to also post this on social media. I will probably make a dedicated post about this if I find the time.

I set the goal and looked at the result at the end. The reviewers did the looking in between.

AI reviewers only get me so far, the real check is players. So every now and then I open the game for a weekend, collect their feedback, iterate and see in the next round whether it worked. This weekend is one of them, free in the browser until Sunday evening:  
[https://pixkrieg.com/](https://pixkrieg.com/)

What do you think of the first iteration based of player feedback shown in the video?
